cohort: 154 term infants admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit for respiratory distress, hypoglycemia, maternal chorioamnionitis, and suspected neonatal sepsis
finding: In sick term neonates, early nasopharyngeal colonization is dominated by Staphylococcus epidermidis and is enhanced by rupture of membrane and reduced by maternal group B Streptococcus colonization, whereas rectal colonization is dominated by E. coli and decreases with cesarean section.
mod_finding: Cesarean section decreases the rectal colonization, which is composed of E. coli as the predominant microorganism.
